newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Aucklanders pay 30 pct more for insurance -council.
newsitem.headline: Aucklanders pay 30 pct more for insurance -council.

text.p: Aucklanders pay at least one third more for their house, contents and motor vehicle insurance than the rest of New Zealand, according to an Insurance Council survey released on Monday.

Council chief executive David Sargeant said the survey of companies asked what effect burglary and theft claims were having on the cost of insurance and how Auckland compared to the rest of the country.

"The results are not good for those living in the Auckland region. All companies who responded to the survey (representing 92 percent of the market) said that the trend for crime related claims in Auckland had increased over the last three years -- one company said by 36 percent," Sargeant said in a statement.
"The cost of claims was between 36 and 52 percent higher in Auckland than elsewhere in the country and the number of burglary and theft claims higher by at least 45 percent."

For the year ended 1996, theft and burglary in Auckland cost insurance companies NZ$42 million in home and contents claims, compared to approximately $28 million for the rest of the country. Motor vehicle claims in Auckland cost $25 million in 1996.
"This is making it more expensive to insure Aucklanders and results in their premiums being at least 30 percent higher than anywhere else in the country," Sergeant said.
